name: Gunnshy Peak Standard Route (Barclay Lake Approach)

approach_variants.name: Barclay Lake spur road to the east ridge
approach_variants.notes: There is no official trail. From a spur road near the Barclay Lake trailhead a faint climbers' path heads east into the forest and leads most of the way up. Cross Barclay Creek on logs, leave the old roadbed, and take steep zigzags through the southern slope to a headwall around 3,600 ft. The path then veers east beneath cliff bands and makes a short steep drop into a gully where water dribbles off the rock overhead — dry by late summer, a real flow in winter and spring. Above it cairns lead onto moderate ground, then meadows along the east side of Tailgunner's south ridge to a saddle near 5,400 ft.
hazards: Faint, unmarked climbers' path with sustained route-finding
Slick rock in the seasonal waterfall gully
Heavy slide alder and devil's club if you drift north out of the correct line
Loose rock and exposure on the summit block
Icy, avalanche-prone open slopes in winter and spring
approach_variants.baseFinding: The scrambling starts where the traverse tops out on the east ridge at about 5,950 ft, and three separate identification problems stand between the car and it. At the bottom, an old fire pit on the spur road has been used as the marker for the path start and may no longer be there — look for the boot-worn line heading east into the forest rather than for the fire pit itself, and do not take the maintained lake trail. Above the waterfall gully, where cairns lead out onto moderate ground, the standard error is to head north into heavy slide alder and devil's club instead of continuing east beneath a buttress; if you are fighting devil's club you have gone the wrong way. Past the saddle below Tailgunner and Wing, bypass Point 5,760 by dropping roughly two hundred feet eastward around it rather than going over the top. From there a rising traverse above Gunn Lake through talus and heather brings you onto the crest near 5,950 ft. You are at the base when the traverse ends on the ridge and everything left is a short, exposed class 2-3 scramble on the summit block.

waypoints.name: Barclay Lake Trailhead (FR-6024)
waypoints.directions: From Monroe, drive east on US-2 to Baring and, near milepost 41-42 across from the convenience store, turn left (north) onto 635th Place NE. Cross the railroad tracks and continue about 0.3 mile to a junction, keep left on 635th Place NE for another 0.1 mile, and the road becomes Forest Road 6024 (Barclay Creek Road). Follow roughly 3.9 to 4.3 miles of gravel to the Barclay Lake Trailhead, watching for potholes and rough patches — AWD or 4x4 is recommended after wet weather. There is a vault toilet and parking for about 20 vehicles, and a Northwest Forest Pass is required.

waypoints.name: Ridge Junction (Gunn-Barclay Divide, above waterfall gully)
waypoints.directions: From the spur road near the trailhead, take the faint climbers' path east into the forest rather than the maintained lake trail. Cross Barclay Creek on logs, leave the old roadbed and zigzag steeply up to a headwall at about 3,600 ft. The path veers east beneath cliff bands and drops briefly into the waterfall gully; climb steeply out the far side to where cairns lead onto moderate ground.

waypoints.name: Gunnshy Peak Summit
waypoints.directions: Keep heading east beneath a buttress, not north into slide alder and devil's club, and follow cairns through meadows along Tailgunner's south ridge to the saddle near 5,400 ft. Bypass Point 5,760 by dropping about 200 ft around its east side, make a rising traverse above Gunn Lake through talus and heather to the east ridge near 5,950 ft, then traverse west along and just south of the crest, scrambling to the summit.
